title: Atomic-Scale In Situ ADF-STEM Observation of MoS2 Lithiation
content: Intercalation reactions of atoms such as Li are of crucial importance in materials science, with applications spanning catalysts, capacitors, and batteries. The migration of atoms into host materials is often accompanied by local structural changes at the atomic and nanoscale, necessitating in situ observation to elucidate the dynamics of these changes. At the atomic scale, a promising imaging technique is in situ high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM), which has been successfully used, for example, to visualize the movement of the reaction front during the lithiation process of MoS2 [1]. However, it is worth noting that interpreting the image contrast of HRTEM is not always straightforward, highlighting the need to explore alternative imaging techniques. One such alternative is annular dark-field (ADF) scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) [2], which provides more directly interpretable incoherent images. However, to the best of our knowledge, atomic-scale in situ STEM for lithiation processes has not yet been achieved, limiting the advancement of electron microscopy studies on dynamic lithiation processes. In this study, we used ADF-STEM for atomic-scale in situ observation of the MoS2 lithiation process induced by electron irradiation.
